why.heading: Why Port Alder homeowners call us back
why.html:
Harbourview County has two very different kinds of plumbing. Down by the harbour, many homes still run cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals from the 1960s, and the salt air is hard on exposed copper. Up the valley in Cedar Falls and Millbrook, newer subdivisions sit on well water with enough iron and hardness to scale a water heater in a few years. We see both every week, so we bring the right tools for the street we're on.

We would rather fix the cause than come back. That's why a backed-up drain gets a camera run after it's cleared, and why a failed water heater gets a water test before we recommend a replacement.

items.q: Do you charge a call-out fee?
items.a: There is a diagnostic fee for each visit, and it's credited to the repair if you go ahead with it. We tell you the fee on the phone before booking.

items.q: How fast can you get to Millbrook?
items.a: Millbrook is about 25 minutes from our shop. For an active leak we aim to be there within two hours, day or night.

items.q: Can you work on well-water systems?
items.a: Yes. We service pressure tanks, softeners and the water heaters that sit downstream of them, which is where hard well water does most of its damage.
